correctness.rationale: All 28 exact line equations are individually checked as bitangents, with no denominators in residue characteristics at least seven; smoothness is proved from the gradient. Norms of all 3240 nonzero line-triple determinants confine incidence changes to seven primes, and exact finite-field enumeration gives complete crossing distributions there. Frobenius acts by two explicit sign changes on coefficients and on all incident-line subsets, giving exact rational fixed-crossing and rational fixed-component counts; the proof converts these to all extension point counts and a closed rational zeta function. Direct brute-force point counts over seven prime fields match. Python source in the package was run successfully; no finite sample is taken to establish the all-prime theorem.

At the seven primes the new exact reductions respectively have (252,24,9) or (288,12,9) crossings, and Frobenius incidence determines (4q+1), (16q-71), (28q-299) or (28q-311) prime-field counts, depending on signs.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Specializing the published parameter-discriminant factors supplies an exact upper bound and natural candidates for exceptional reduction primes; this part is not independently original. It does not by itself supply the precise modular incidence supports, the rational fixed-line incidences at crossings, or the complete arithmetic zeta function, which requires new exact determinant and Frobenius calculations. Existing rational-line counts alone cannot settle the union count, since rational points can arise at intersections of conjugate nonrational lines.

originality.rationale: The claim is the complete Frobenius point-count and zeta classification of the reduced 28-line union, not the already-known 28 bitangent equations, the complex 324-node/9-quadruple profile, the Ciani parameter discriminant, or the finite-field number of rational bitangent lines. The published universal complex discriminant has explicit factors whose value at parameter three yields the same seven candidate primes, so that prime list alone is covered and explicitly not offered as novelty. The required geometric-to-arithmetic crossing support, Frobenius-fixed incidence corrections, uniform extension point counts and rational zeta function are absent from the inspected closely relevant records. Prime-field point counts were independently recomputed. Priority remains provisional against genuinely unindexed texts.
residual_risks: Unindexed classical or contemporary explicit zeta computations of exactly the reduced 28-bitangent divisor may exist.

The universal complex Ciani discriminant and finite-field bitangent splitting equations make the new invariant computationally accessible; its novelty is the complete incidence/Frobenius derivation and zeta formula, not the primitive data.

value.rationale: The reduced union of all 28 bitangents is a canonical arithmetic boundary divisor attached to a classical genus-three quartic. The uniform all-prime and all-extension Hasse–Weil zeta function is a natural exact invariant not determined by the known complex incidence counts or bitangent splitting types alone. The distinction between geometric triple-point degeneration at p=7 and unchanged prime-field count is a substantive rational-versus-geometric boundary phenomenon, not an arbitrary numeric slice or cheap reparameterization.
